incidents.victim: Government officials, military personnel & journalists (US, Europe, Ukraine)
incidents.vector: Phishing messages impersonating messaging-app support trick high-value targets into surrendering verification codes, account PINs and backup recovery keys to hijack Signal, WhatsApp and Telegram accounts.
incidents.impact: FBI/CISA and Ukraine's SBU say Russian intelligence clusters are running an ongoing campaign to take over the messaging accounts of officials, military personnel and journalists to read sensitive communications; the apps' encryption itself was not broken.

incidents.vector: Phishing emails carrying malicious Remote Desktop Protocol configuration files deploy the StockStay backdoor, disguised as PDF readers or calculator apps and often sent from compromised university and diplomatic accounts.
incidents.impact: Google detailed StockStay, a Kazuar-derived espionage implant in active development since 2022, used to spy on Ukrainian government and defense bodies, with earlier samples also seen in Italy, the Netherlands, Poland and Germany.

incidents.victim: John Bolton (former US National Security Advisor)
incidents.vector: An Iran-linked actor compromised Bolton's personal email account, which he had used to store classified 'diary' entries, after he left office in 2019.
incidents.impact: Revealed in Bolton's June 26 guilty plea to retaining national defense information; DOJ said the hacked personal account held material classified up to TOP SECRET, exposing it to a foreign adversary.

incidents.vector: 2022 credential-stuffing attack reused breached username/password pairs to take over accounts; attackers added their own payment methods to drain funds and sold remaining access through a cybercrime shop.
incidents.impact: Roughly 60,000 customer accounts compromised and about $600,000 stolen; the third and final defendant ('Snoopy') was sentenced June 25 to 18 months and $1.3M restitution.

incidents.vector: Attacker made rogue SD-WAN peering connections, manipulated default admin passwords, then exploited zero-day CVE-2026-20245 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager via a malicious CSV upload to create a root-level 'troot' account.
incidents.impact: Mandiant says the actor gained full root control of the provider's SD-WAN orchestrator, potentially exposing internal corporate traffic, and used extensive anti-forensic cleanup so the full scope remains unclear.

incidents.vector: Data was taken from a third-party vendor that managed the agency's mobile device management platform; the breach was tied to a wave of attacks on Ivanti EPMM servers last year.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole the names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence service officials, exposing personnel of a national security agency.

incidents.vector: The 'World Leaks' extortion group listed the company on its leak site, claiming theft of internal documents.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed a breach after the group claimed over 200,000 stolen documents allegedly containing sensitive data on Apple and Tesla electronic components.

incidents.vector: SIM-swapping and SMS/voice phishing to steal employee credentials and bypass MFA, enabling network intrusion and extortion.
incidents.impact: Two UK members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty to the August 2024 attack that crippled Transport for London; the group's wider spree hit 47 US entities and reaped over $115M in ransoms.

incidents.victim: Klue customers (LastPass, Snyk & other security firms)
incidents.vector: Attackers used a compromised legacy integration credential to access market-intelligence platform Klue, stole customers' OAuth tokens, then connected to their Salesforce instances to download data.
incidents.impact: At least eight companies, including LastPass and Snyk, confirmed data stolen from Salesforce via the Klue supply-chain breach; a group calling itself 'Icarus' is extorting victims and the list is expected to grow.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate users (government, critical infrastructure, multinationals)
incidents.vector: Mass password-spraying (~1.16B attempts) plus interception of traffic through firewalls with a custom 'FortigateSniffer' script, then offline GPU cracking of exported config files to recover plaintext admin and VPN credentials.
incidents.impact: Valid credentials for ~73,932 FortiGate firewalls across 194 countries leaked in the 'FortiBleed' campaign; a Turkish NATO defense contractor is among confirmed victims (classified documents allegedly exfiltrated), access is being sold on, and infrastructure remains active.

incidents.victim: Oracle PeopleSoft users (Council of Europe, Kodak, Ralph Lauren, universities)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unpatched zero-day vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft ERP to steal large volumes of data, followed by extortion via a dark-web leak site.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters has been listing and extorting a growing roster of victims, including the Council of Europe (297GB claimed), Kodak (2.2M customers claimed), Ralph Lauren, JCPenney and several universities; Oracle had not patched the flaw at time of reporting.

incidents.vector: Breach of the agency's hunting and fishing license registration systems; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal details of more than three million license registrants were stolen, including government IDs, driver's licenses and home addresses.

incidents.vector: A malicious or pre-installed SDK ('Popa', tied to the Vo1d/Badbox botnet) on cheap Android TV boxes silently enrolls home internet connections into a residential proxy pool.
incidents.impact: Researchers (Krebs, Qurium, Synthient, HUMAN) linked the Popa botnet, which forces millions of TV boxes to relay traffic for ad fraud, account takeovers and mass scraping, to NetNut, a proxy provider owned by Israeli firm Alarum Technologies, which disputes the findings.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of critical FortiSandbox flaws CVE-2026-39808 (OS command injection) and CVE-2026-39813 (path traversal), bypassing authentication and escalating privileges to run arbitrary commands.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed dozens of exploitation events from multiple independent operators across nine countries against the trusted security appliance; reconnaissance activity typically precedes heavier attack waves.

incidents.victim: North American medical, academic & military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploited externally facing REDCap research servers, deployed the custom INFINITERED backdoor to harvest credentials, then abused Google Workspace content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive email.
incidents.impact: Google (GTIG/Mandiant) found the group UNC6508 had lurked undetected since September 2023, stealing data on AI, defense, uncrewed systems and medical research; the actor remains active and likely has many more victims.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into parts of the company's internal network; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The Danish pharma giant (maker of Ozempic and Wegovy) said attackers accessed internal systems and copied some sensitive data, including patient PII, prompting it to take systems offline.

incidents.victim: WordPress sites using Awesome Motive plugins (~1.2M sites)
incidents.vector: Malicious code was inserted into legitimate JavaScript of three Awesome Motive plugins (OptinMonster, TrustPulse, PushEngage); it waits for an admin login, creates a rogue admin account and installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million websites were backdoored through the plugin supply-chain compromise, giving attackers persistent administrative access.

incidents.vector: Attackers used the AUR 'adopt' mechanism to take over abandoned/orphaned community packages, then modified install scripts to pull a malicious npm/Bun package that deployed a rootkit and credential-harvesting infostealer.
incidents.impact: More than 1,900 Arch Linux AUR packages were hijacked over a weekend to infect users with a rootkit and infostealer that grabs browser, developer and Electron-app secrets; the number of affected downloads is still unknown.

incidents.victim: Major Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, Export Development Bank)
incidents.vector: Attack reportedly targeted communications infrastructure shared by the four banks; technical details not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks were knocked offline over a weekend; intelligence sources believe Israeli hackers were likely responsible. The banks said no customer data was accessed.
